evidence: Scoped source-level pinning Pass. Workbook Quality Checks D48 and skill quality-checks.md:187-189 explicitly permit public networking and require neither temperature nor prompt-version markers; the older Internal Quality Checks D48 wording is superseded by this current profile. Frozen task/task.toml:31-36 selects REWARDKIT_JUDGE="claude-code" and REWARDKIT_MODEL="z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx" with the exact shared verifier environment. Parsed comparison to frozen rules/projects/webdev-task-template/task.toml confirms equality. All five judge.toml files use the matching claude-code fallback and Playwright MCP command with --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium (lines 1-12); none overrides model, temperature or reasoning effort. task/tests/Dockerfile:16-21 pins claude-code@2.1.281, codex@0.151.0 and @playwright/mcp@0.0.79; line 31 pins harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7. Lines 33-38 install Chromium through that pinned MCP package's bundled Playwright CLI and link the absolute browser path used by every dimension. Direct byte comparison shows the Dockerfile is identical to the frozen template (SHA256 72998ab8ef0e4225e63b88fccdb754943c54022e25da355035efe7f759a55fdd). Both shared tools are also byte-identical: score.py SHA256 13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e; restart_mcp.py SHA256 03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5. No graded calendar/date rule was found in the criteria, seed or relevant public instructions, so a fixed calendar clock is not applicable. behaviour.md:9,19,21 defines elapsed execution budgets/durations/debounce. functional/prompt.md:15,399,406-409 and 477-487 measures actual browser-action lifetimes with explicit margins and successful controls; it does not compare results with the run date. Date.now() at prompt.md:36 supplies a unique local-network probe token only. server.js:73,85 writes display timestamps, while prompt.md:440,444 explicitly ignores collection order and display-only timestamps when comparing required restart state. Verified all hashes in the indexed current_source_checks, current_cli_admission and unchanged_actual_browser_mcp_control groups. The relevant historical MCP source binding matches current task.toml, tests/Dockerfile and both shared tools; observations.json (SHA256 ba10bfd001272d5f0db2f2d7cfdf6fadf6e6652dd1fe2b1d6fe49aff5067b181) records the exact configured MCP argv and Playwright server version 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-05 with a completed browser operation. This is tool-operation evidence only. Current cli-arguments/RESULTS.json (SHA256 49ed2616cf73244f9d779e12651a4d02fe19ae7da6b1af417f0f70778c015c69) binds every current judge/prompt hash and confirms RewardKit 0.1.7, but explicitly says provider_invoked=false and judge_launched=false. The raw index explicitly leaves full configured judge completion/workload, Oracle grade, Luna score and empirical reward behavior unmeasured. This row establishes the specified source pins, not repeatable model scores, full judge launch/grading or private checker execution. Those missing measurements remain separate clearance risks and are not waived here.
counterexample: Considered a broken app that reports a constant 0 ms while its delayed timer runs: functional/prompt.md:399 explicitly rejects a constant label and requires a measured delayed lifetime distinct from a short Run, so the timing policy offers no date-based escape. Considered a conforming alternative that uses seconds and rounded durations, a different debounce delay below the public limit, or changing display timestamps: prompt.md:399,406-409 accepts units/rounding and measures that app's own debounce delay; prompt.md:440,444 excludes display timestamps from required state. No wrong-grade counterexample was established for row 47. These are source-level adversarial checks, not newly executed app variants.
